exposure: Training and deployment of non-physician clinicians (NPCs) called medical licentiates (ML) to perform surgery
Patients who underwent surgery by MLs
Patients who underwent surgery by surgically active medical doctors (MDs)
outcome: Number of other major surgical procedures
cohort: Patients in 16 rural hospitals in Zambia
finding: The training and deployment of MLs in rural hospitals in Zambia led to a significant increase in the number of caesarean sections performed and did not result in a significant difference in postoperative wound infection rates compared to MDs.
mod_finding: The deployment of MLs led to a significant increase in the number of caesarean sections performed in the intervention hospitals.
